title: Connect the board power adapter
step: Plug a plus 12 volt power adapter into the 2.10 millimeter barrel jack, which supports 12 to 36 volts, using the Type-C to barrel adapter if needed.
look_for: 2.10 mm barrel jack connector labeled JPWR

title: Connect USB0 for software flashing
step: Connect a USB Type-C cable from the USB0 port on the board to your host device to allow software flashing.

title: Connect the debug UART cable
step: Connect a micro-USB cable between the micro-USB port on the board and your host computer for the debug serial console.

title: Check Ubuntu host serial ports
step: Install screen on your Ubuntu host if needed and list the USB serial devices to confirm four ports appear.

title: Open the main serial console
step: Open the second serial device, ttyUSB1, at 115200 baud with screen after ensuring no other process uses it.

title: Log in to the console
step: Press Enter to bring up the login prompt and log in with the event credentials.

title: Verify the Ubuntu OS version
step: Check the OS release file to confirm the board is running Ubuntu 24.04.3 LTS.

title: Check the Linux kernel version
step: Run uname with the all flag to verify the Qualcomm Linux kernel version and aarch64 architecture.

title: Connect to a Wi-Fi network
step: Use nmcli in station mode with your network name and password to connect the board to Wi-Fi.

title: Find the Wi-Fi IP address
step: Verify the Wi-Fi connection and read the assigned IP address on interface wlp1s0.

title: Connect Ethernet and check IP
step: Plug an Ethernet cable into the RJ45 port on the board and check interface end0 for its IP address.
look_for: RJ45 Ethernet port on the board

title: Connect to the board via SSH
step: From a host on the same network, connect over SSH as user ubuntu at the board IP address and log in with the event credentials.

title: Connect a DisplayPort monitor
step: Before powering on, connect a monitor to DisplayPort0 or JEDP1 using an active Mini DisplayPort to DisplayPort cable or active HDMI adapter.
look_for: DisplayPort0 (JEDP0) or JEDP1 port, then Ubuntu server or desktop screen

title: DS1 Green Debug LED
step: DS1 is a green debug LED that stays off during normal operation and blinks briefly at power on, so power cycle the board if it stays lit.
look_for: DS1 label, green LED on mainboard

title: DS8 and DS9 Ethernet LEDs
step: DS8 and DS9 are green Ethernet LEDs that glow solid when a link is established and blink during data transfer, so check the cable if they stay off.
look_for: DS8 and DS9 labels, green LEDs on mainboard

title: DS10 Green Power Regulator LED
step: DS10 is a green LED showing that the three point three volt regulator is supplying power normally, so inspect the power rails if it stays off at boot.
look_for: DS10 label, green LED on mainboard

title: DS11 Orange Regulator Status LED
step: DS11 is an orange LED for the three point three volt regulator that lights during self test and signals a warning or fault if lit during normal boot.
look_for: DS11 label, orange LED on mainboard

title: LED1 Software Controlled RGB LED
step: LED1 is a software controlled RGB LED driven by GPIO pins that can show green at boot and custom status patterns once the operating system is ready.
look_for: LED1 label, green LED on mainboard

title: Main Power On Off Switch
step: This side mounted slide switch is the main power control, so flip it to turn the board on or off and power cycle the device.
look_for: Side-mounted slide or toggle switch at position 25

title: Reserved GPIO 6 Push Button
step: This small push button connects to GPIO 6 and is currently inactive because it is reserved for a future software feature.

title: Red EDL and Fastboot Switch
step: SW2 is the large red DIP switch for boot modes, and flipping switch three on puts both domains into forced USB download mode for flashing software.
look_for: Large red DIP switch labeled SW2 on mainboard

title: Small Mezzanine Routing DIP Switches
step: These smaller DIP switches below the red switch route interfaces between mainboard connectors and mezzanine cards, and all functions work with them left in the off default.
look_for: Smaller DIP switches below the large red switch, labeled SW1, SW3, SW4, SW7, SW8, SW9

title: USB0 SuperSpeed Type C Port
step: USB0 is a USB 3 SuperSpeed Type C port supporting both host and device modes, so plug in a Type C cable for peripherals or device mode.

title: USB1 Host Type C Port
step: USB1 is a USB 3 SuperSpeed Type C port that operates in host mode, so use it to connect USB peripherals such as cameras or hubs.

title: USB2 Micro USB 2 Port
step: USB2 is a USB 2 high speed micro USB port supporting both host and device modes, so connect a micro USB cable for data or peripherals.

title: JFAN CPU Cooler Fan Header
step: JFAN is the PWM fan connector on the mainboard where the bottom mounted CPU cooler fan plugs in for automatic temperature controlled cooling.

title: JLS1 40 Pin Expansion Header
step: JLS1 is the 40 pin low speed expansion header providing three point three volt GPIOs, CAN, UART, I2C, and SPI, so attach external sensors or jumpers carefully.

title: Dual RJ45 2.5G Ethernet Ports
step: These dual RJ45 ports provide two point five gigabit Ethernet networking, so plug in standard Ethernet cables for wired network access.

title: Mini DisplayPort Video Output Ports
step: These two mini DisplayPort connectors output video with one supporting multi stream transport, so connect the included mini DisplayPort to DisplayPort cable for external displays.

title: Mainboard Micro SD Card Slot
step: This micro SD card slot provides removable storage on the mainboard when switch SW1 3 is off, so insert a micro SD card for extra storage.

title: Mainboard PCIe x4 Expansion Slot
step: This PCIe four lane slot on the mainboard accepts expansion cards, such as the included PCIe edge card adapter for NVMe storage.

title: Four MIPI CSI Camera Connectors
step: These four CSI camera interfaces connect C PHY or D PHY cameras to the mainboard when the corresponding SW1 switches are off.

title: Mainboard Power Input Barrel Plug
step: This power plug supplies mainboard power, so connect the included power supply using the Type C to barrel plug adapter before turning on the power switch.
